newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle trade light at $66 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle trade light at $66 - feedlots.

text.p: Light trade at a steady $66 per cwt was reported in Kansas feedlot cattle on Wednesday in largely "clean-up" type trade after heavy volume Tuesday, feedlot sources said.
Showlists were largely mopped up on Tuesday with USDA estimating week-to-date sales in Texas/west Oklahoma of 108,900 head and in Kansas of 82,600 head.

"They (packers) have got enough bought there is no reason for them to give $67 this week because that would set them up to have to give more than that next week," one Texas dealer said, noting feedlots would not accept less than $66.
Dealers noted that the $66 paid on Tuesday was up $2 from the bulk of trade last week, with rising beef prices contributing to the market's advance.
USDA boxed beef cut-out values, as of 1130 CDT, were up $0.78 to $0.07 per cwt and prices have now risen around $8.50 per cwt since the upward trend began on July 11.
